title: Factorization of the absolute Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $p$ is prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k$ is a fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. As in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], let $\sigma:k\to k$ be $b\mapsto b^q$, put $g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$, and let $\Phi=\Phi_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$, where $\Phi_0$ is the absolute $q$-power Frobenius of $X_0$. For every integer $m\geq1$, the absolute $q^m$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]
$\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X:X\to X$, whose affine incarnation on the base change of any affine chart $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq X_0$ is $u\otimes b\mapsto u^{q^m}\otimes b^{q^m}$, factors as an equality of $k_0$-scheme morphisms

$$
\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X=g_\sigma^m\circ\Phi^m=\Phi^m\circ g_\sigma^m.
$$

proof.text: Absolute Frobenius is natural in every scheme morphism: use Scheme.Hom.ext, its identity underlying map, and map_pow on each section ring. The same extensionality proves F_(n+r) = F_n followed by F_r and F_0 = identity, since x^(p^(n+r)) = (x^(p^r))^(p^n). Induction gives F_(a*m) = (F_a)^m. These sectionwise arguments also apply to zero rings and nonreduced schemes.

proof.text: Let sigma be the inverse of geometric field Frobenius. Its definition identifies it with arithmetic field Frobenius, x maps to x^q. By ext_to_Spec and GammaSpecIso naturality, the absolute p^a-power Frobenius on Spec k equals Spec(sigma): on global sections the equality is map_pow and p^a=q=card(k_0). Use the relativeFrobenius_projections and galoisMap_projections equations: P fixes the second projection and acts by model Frobenius on the first; S fixes the first projection and acts by Spec(sigma) on the second. Naturality from step 1 gives precisely the two projections of absolute F_a. The universal property pullback.hom_ext therefore proves F_a=P followed by S and F_a=S followed by P, hence P and S commute.

proof.text: Raise each one-step factorization to the m-th power. Since P and S commute, Commute.mul_pow gives (PS)^m=P^m S^m in both orders. Step 1 identifies the left side with absolute F_(a*m), and schemeFrobeniusIterate is by definition P^m. Translate End multiplication back into categorical composition to obtain exactly both conjuncts of the statement, with all original hypotheses retained.
